newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's SIDANKO plans ADR, bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Russia's SIDANKO plans ADR, bond issues.

text.p: Russian oil company SIDANKO plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in early 1998 and a convertible bond later this year, company Vice-President Dmitry Maslov said on Monday.

"Having completed the issue of convertible bonds (by the end of the year) and having converted them into a (single company) share, our programme is to carry out a further share issue which will be aimed at foreign investors above all," Maslov said. "(This) will be done most probably through issuing level one ADRs."

OAO Sibirskaya Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) said last year it would issue bonds in 1997 and look at the possibility of increasing share capital to 26.17 billion roubles from 9.3 billion.
"A bond issue is seen as the most effective mechanism for converting the company into a single share," a company statement said on Monday.
SIDANKO said it had increased its share of charter capital in all subsidiary companies except AO Kondpetroleum to over 75 percent from 38 percent (or 50.7 percent of voting shares) previously.
SIDANKO's main production units are Chernogorneft, Varyoganneftegaz and Kondpetroleum.

SIDANKO produced 20.81 million tonnes (416,000 barrels per day) of crude oil in 1996 excluding joint venture output, down from 22.87 million (457,000 bpd) in 1995. It ranked sixth largest of Russia's oil companies by production last year.
